properties.title: MgO Abundance · Clementine 1D-CNN (Qiu et al., 2025)
properties.authors: Denggao Qiu, Jianguo Yan, Bin Liu
properties.processing:lineage: Clementine UVVIS DIM Mosaic (5 bands: 415, 750, 900, 950, 1000 nm, 100 m/pixel) combined with OMAT as a 6-element input vector. 1D CNN: two Conv1D layers (32 filters, kernel=2, ReLU), MaxPooling1D (pool=2), Dense(64, ReLU), single linear output. L2 regularization (0.001). Adam optimizer (lr=0.01), max 400 epochs, early stopping (patience=30), z-score normalization. Trained on 49 ground-truth points from Apollo, Luna, and Chang'E missions including Chang'E-6. MgO cannot be estimated from classical equation models. Lowest LOOCV R² of the five oxides (0.755); use for spatial targeting rather than quantitative estimates. R²=0.96+ on training set.
properties.lri:data_use_note: MgO is the numerator of the Mg# index and an indicator of magma evolution. High MgO (and high Mg#) signals primitive, less-differentiated material — typically mantle-derived ultramafic rocks. Lowest LOOCV R² of the five oxides (0.755); prefer spatial/relative use over quantitative absolute values. Best used in combination with Mg# and FeO to identify olivine-rich or mantle-exposed terrains (e.g., central peaks of large craters, SPA basin floor).
properties.lri:quality_note_short: 1D CNN inversion from Clementine UVVIS, calibrated with Chang'E-6 samples. LOOCV R²=0.755 (lowest of the five oxides). Global mean 6.90 wt%. Use with caution in quantitative estimates; stronger for spatial targeting. Numerator of the Mg# derived index.
properties.lri:quality_note: MgO abundance derived from 1D CNN inversion of Clementine UVVIS 5-band reflectance (Qiu et al. 2025, Communications Earth & Environment). CNN-only product — not derivable from classical equation models. LOOCV R²=0.755 is the lowest of the five oxides, reflecting the more complex and indirect spectral signature of MgO in multi-band optical data. Global mean 6.90 wt%; bimodal distribution with modes at 5.11 wt% (non-maria) and 10.31 wt% (maria). Non-maria mean 6.41 wt%; maria mean 9.42 wt%. MgO content is used to indicate magma evolution: high MgO (>10 wt%) suggests primitive, less-differentiated mantle-derived material such as olivine-rich lithologies or pyroxenites. This map is used as the numerator in the Mg# calculation (molar Mg/(Mg+Fe)). Key resource consideration: MgO-rich regions are potential sources of magnesium metal. Interpret spatial patterns with confidence, but apply a ~20-30% uncertainty margin to absolute wt% values given the lower LOOCV performance.
